cap: Withholding water raises plasma osmolality, which should release ADH and concentrate the urine. Normal people and those with primary polydipsia do concentrate, so desmopressin adds little. In both forms of diabetes insipidus the urine stays dilute; desmopressin then separates them, because it replaces missing ADH in central DI but cannot act on a kidney that ignores it in nephrogenic DI.
teach: Primary polydipsia often concentrates less than normal at first, because months of heavy drinking wash solute out of the renal medulla; the curve still rises during deprivation, which is the feature that separates it from diabetes insipidus. The test is stopped early if plasma osmolality or sodium climbs above the normal range, because by then ADH should be maximal.
